I read pp. 90–93 and the Lean statements. Signs and operators match: graphDr p_m = g_r − ρP − A_0(g_r − ρP); streamGamma = γ_d − R⁻¹A_0(Rγ_d); streamBeta(ε•w) = −ε∂_ZΨ; I_c = pastIntegral − χ·totalIntegral as in (8.9). Every clause is stated or recoverable in a few lines, mostly in the moving √q gauge. Three clauses exist only on a fixed shell, Δβ ∈ M_{α+1} only for specific sources, and slow-support retention only as fibre locality; each has a written recovery that the repository itself uses elsewhere. No hypothesis is vacuous. Both skeptics reached the same verdict; the only dissent concerns which declarations best cover the Y-independent clause, and I added those.

findings.summary: No single declaration states Proposition 8.3. Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas, some on a fixed shell (PressureStream, MeanRankUpdate) and some in the moving √q gauge (VariableGaugeMean, GaugeAliasDecay, MovingMomentBounds, GaugeMassPreservation).

(8.13b) and the zero Y-mean of A_0(g_r − ρP) are stated only for a fixed shell with a globally smooth periodic source. The Y-independent clause has a slice lemma and a moving-gauge instance for the rank source, but no general moving-gauge statement.
Δβ ∈ M_{α+1} is stated with the ε factor only for specific sources (temporal stage, rank stage). For a general γ_d ∈ M_α the Lean states only −∂_ZΨ ∈ M_α for a fixed direction w.
Retention of the (Z,T)-projection of the source support is not stated as a support lemma. The Lean states the stronger FiberLocal property; only radial support is stated directly.

The Lean fixes concrete choices the paper leaves free: ρ is a normed ContDiffBump in the middle half of the same [a,b] used for the source shell, and the cutoff is interiorCutoff(a^d, b^d) in the power chart.

Judge-added. Flatness is stated as MeanClass β for every β in chart variables, at the actual radial frequency with periodicity and index-gap hypotheses, not as an O(q^N) bound on physical derivatives.
